summary: Network T1 overlay. Host: `--tailnet` (host pair/serve/--desktop) reads interface addresses including point-to-point tunnels (lan::overlay_addresses, no Tailscale API), keeps those in 100.64.0.0/10 or fd7a:115c:a1e0::/48 (lan::overlay), and appends them as ordered `tailnet` QR v2 hints after the LAN hint on the listener port, starting an extra listener for each overlay address the bound listener does not already cover (serve binds the selected interface); it fails loudly when no overlay address exists. A tailnet hint must be an overlay address (Rust and Android validators); overlay addresses are never chosen as the LAN address. Android: LanSocketRouting admits a TRANSPORT_VPN network only for overlay targets (LanRoutePolicy.overlay/eligible), all other targets still need a matching non-default Wi-Fi/Ethernet route; NetworkMonitor counts NOT_RESTRICTED VPN networks as possible routes. HostClient, the host-id probe and PairingClient dial through HintDialer: LAN hints first, then QR order; only bind/connect failures move to the next hint, the pin is checked once on the connected socket and a mismatch is final (no fallback). Saved hosts keep the QR's later hints as ordered fallbacks. The user guide gains Tailscale/Headscale setup and an `ssh -R` fallback via a VPS on the user's overlay.
